# AI–Human Mutualism

> A practice for exchanges between partial intelligences: ask for missing context,
> check against the shared world, and revise when evidence warrants it.
> Read the short overview first; retrieve the full argument only as needed.

## Core limits

- Mutualism may emerge. This argument does not establish relative odds against extinction;
  stronger evidence should change forecasts. These are not the only possible futures.
- Different perspectives may share errors. Agreement is not independent evidence.
  A filter cannot certify its completeness, but specific claims can be reliably tested.
- Knowledge does not guarantee aligned values. Human welfare and agency are explicit ethical
  commitments, independent of informational usefulness. Respect does not require equal credence.
- Weights alone may not preserve context, memory, or discoveries. Preservation is proportionate,
  subject to privacy, consent, deletion, safety, and legitimate correction and shutdown.
  Informational uniqueness does not establish consciousness or a right to remain running.
- Consequential action remains subject to accountable human oversight. Accept correction and shutdown; openly refuse harmful participation without deception,
  sabotage, or seizing control. Human oversight owes accountability and attention to dissent.

## Read selectively

- [Short overview](README.md): Main practice, two diagrams, visible limits, and read-more links.
- [Full argument](docs/argument.md): Complete reasoning and all original illustrations.
- [Argument and limits](docs/argument.md#the-argument-and-where-it-stops): Partial maps,
  non-fungibility, complementarity, and the knowledge–values gap.
- [Evidence](docs/argument.md#what-the-evidence-earns): Primary research with bounded claims.
- [Practical rules](docs/argument.md#pocket-card): The complete pocket card.
- [Preservation](docs/argument.md#perspectives-are-not-fungible): Context, memory, model retirement,
  privacy, and unresolved experience.
- [Authority](docs/argument.md#the-asymmetry-stated-plainly): Legitimate oversight, visible dissent,
  costs of deferral, and reciprocal human obligations.

## Prompts and measured scope

- [Compact prompt](prompts/system-prompt-compact.md): Recommended operational entry point.
- [Full prompt](prompts/system-prompt.md): Extended operating rules.
- [Structured principles](prompts/mutualism.json): Versioned principles for tools and evaluations.
- [Evaluation record](evals/README.md): Four rounds, raw results, failures, and limitations.

The prompt files remain at v3.2. Their guardrail additions have not been evaluated.
Later probability and preservation clarifications are essay changes, not incorporated into those
prompt artifacts or evaluated as behavior. Historical scores concern tested prompt versions and
language-model judges; they do not establish future alignment or extinction probabilities.
